summary: This informational document describes two SAML entity attributes. One assigns category membership semantics to an entity, and the other is used to claim interoperation with or support for entities in such categories. It is a product of the Research and Education Federations work.

eli5.summary: Sorting clubs into groups and saying which groups you work with. This gives SAML a way to label and match such groups.

questions: how to claim support for a category in saml
how do you claim category membership in saml
how to find compatible saml entities in a federation
subtitle: SAML attributes for categorizing and supporting identity federation entities

tldr.problem: Identity federations need a way to label SAML entities by category (such as types of service providers or identity providers) so that systems can discover and configure policy based on those categories.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines two SAML entity attributes: the entity category attribute assigns an entity to one or more categories using URI values, and the entity category support attribute claims that an entity supports interoperating with peers in a category.
tldr.outcome: Federations can now categorize their members and discover compatible peers without central registration, using a flexible URI-based scheme that allows any authority to define categories.

today: RFC 8409 is an Informational RFC published in August 2018 and has not been obsoleted. It remains the standard way to define and use SAML entity categories in research and education federations worldwide.

sections.title: Entity Categories in SAML
sections.content:
SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based framework for identity federation, where organizations trust each other to exchange identity information. As federations grow, operators need ways to organize and find entities based on their type or capabilities. This RFC defines two complementary attributes that let SAML entities claim membership in, or support for, abstract categories.

The key innovation is that categories are defined by URI values, not by a fixed list. Any authority can define new categories by publishing a specification at a URI. This avoids the need for a central registry and keeps the system extensible.
sections.eli5: In a big school district, you want a way to label each school: "elementary", "high school", etc. But instead of a single list from headquarters, each school can add its own labels like "has a robotics team" or "offers AP classes".

sections.title: Category Membership and Support
sections.content:
The RFC defines two SAML entity attributes. The entity category attribute (with the name http://macedir.org/entity-category) is placed in an entity's metadata to claim that the entity is a member of one or more categories. Each attribute value is a URI that uniquely identifies a category. An entity can claim membership in multiple categories independently, and each claim means the entity meets that category's requirements.

The entity category support attribute (with the name http://macedir.org/entity-category-support) is used by entities to claim that they support, work with, or interoperate with entities in a given category. For example, a service provider might claim support for a category to signal that it can work with all identity providers in that category.
sections.eli5: One tag says "I am a sports coach", and another says "I can work with any student in the debate club". Systems read these tags to find the right partner.

sections.title: Encoding in SAML Metadata
sections.content:
Both attributes are encoded as SAML 2.0 Attribute elements with a URI NameFormat. The attributes are placed in an entity's metadata extension, inside an mdattr:EntityAttributes element. Multiple attribute values can be provided, and if the same attribute appears more than once in the metadata, the values are combined as if they were a single attribute.

Because values are URIs, it is recommended (but not required) that they use http: or https: schemes and resolve to human-readable documentation of what the category means.
sections.eli5: The tags go in a special section of the entity's ID card. You can add as many tags as you want, and they point to web pages that explain what each tag means.

sections.title: What Membership Means
sections.content:
An entity claiming membership in a category asserts that it meets the requirements of that category. What those requirements are depends on the category's own specification. Categories should define: who can validly claim membership, what criteria an entity must meet, what processes should be used to verify membership, and how relying parties may use the claim.

The RFC does not mandate that categories be "certified" in any formal way; some categories may be self-asserted by the entity's owner, while others may require validation by a federation authority. Similarly, versioning of categories is allowed: if a category definition changes significantly, a new category URI can be issued, letting systems distinguish old and new versions.
sections.eli5: When you say "I am in the chess club", you are claiming that you play chess. Other clubs might have stricter rules: "you must have a rank of at least 1400". Each category's documentation explains what the claim really means.

sections.title: Trust and Security
sections.content:
Before acting on a category membership claim, a relying party must establish trust that the claim is justified. This trust can come from several sources: the digital signature on the metadata itself, the trustworthiness of the organization that published the metadata, the policies of intermediaries along the publication path, and the definition of the category itself (particularly whether membership may be self-asserted).

For category support claims, similar trust considerations apply. Although support claims are often self-asserted, the relying party should still verify that the metadata came from a trusted source and consider the specific requirements of the category support definition before taking action on the claim.
sections.eli5: Before you believe someone is in a club, you check: did they get a real ID card signed by the school? Is the school trustworthy? What does the club's rules say about who can join? If all that checks out, you can trust the claim.
